concept: Icon is printing on the case made of holes. Every glyph is a pattern of round dots on a seven by seven matrix, the Grille's own field at icon scale, so a symbol reads as part of the same perforated object.

default_to_avoid.pattern: generic line icon set: a two pixel rounded stroke icon pack such as Feather or Material outlined
default_to_avoid.why_not: A stroke pack is the same drawing every app ships, and it shares nothing with the grille field that P4 makes the system's one dot language.

default_to_avoid.pattern: cute pixel face icon set with eyes, smiles and bouncing glyphs
default_to_avoid.why_not: INTAKE rule 6 forbids a bloated round toy, and P6 keeps surfaces still, so a dot glyph stays an exact symbol with no face and no idle motion.

default_to_avoid.pattern: orange accent icon used to mark the active item
default_to_avoid.why_not: P1 keeps orange for the one primary control body, and icons take the ink of the part they sit on instead of a hue of their own.

references.source: Braun L 2 loudspeaker: a square field of round holes on the module grid of the case
Yoto Player dot-matrix face and the N200 dot numerals: figures drawn as round dots on a small matrix (user references, D-006)
apps/lab/icon/index.html: four drawing systems measured at 16, 20 and 24px in light and dark

derivation.consequence: grille pitch is one module step, so holes sit on the same grid as the body's inset
derivation.form: Each glyph sits on a seven by seven matrix whose dot is two thirds of the pitch, the Grille's ratio of an 8px hole on a 12px pitch.

derivation.consequence: holes are circles; their field is a rectangle or circle that nests in the body
derivation.form: Every mark is a round dot in a square field, and status glyphs print their sign as missing dots inside Badge's lamp shapes.

derivation.consequence: printing is flat on the material, with no shadow and no emboss
derivation.form: Dots are flat ink in currentColor with no recess or shadow, because a glyph is printing and a 2px dot cannot hold a light model.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: The glyph has no fill of its own and inherits currentColor, so it is ink on plastic and text.on-accent on the orange key.

derivation.consequence: ink on plastic at ≥4.5:1 in both themes; no tinted text
derivation.form: At 16px the dots grow to four fifths of the pitch so every dot reaches 3:1 against the plastic on a 1x screen.

derivation.consequence: no entry choreography, no idle animation; transitions only on state
derivation.form: A glyph never animates; when a state changes the key swaps its name and the new pattern prints at once.

derivation.consequence: labels name their control through aria-labelledby, and the model name is never the only identifier
derivation.form: A glyph is hidden from assistive tech by default because its key carries the name; a label prop makes it role img with that name.

options.name: dot matrix 7 × 7, dot two thirds of the pitch at every size
dot matrix 9 × 9, dot two thirds of the pitch
hairline stroke on the module grid
dot matrix 7 × 7, dots grow to four fifths of the pitch at 16px

variants.reason: Measured at 16px on a 1x screen, D brings every dot to 3:1 on the plastic in light and dark while A reaches 93% and B 58%; C is the generic line pack and leaves the grille field that P4 sets, so the dot form passes and no stroke variant is offered.

root.why: The glyph is a square field of dots on one pitch, sized from the control icon tokens so it nests in a key.

sm.why: The small size draws its dots larger in the same field so each dot keeps 3:1 against the plastic on a 1x screen.

md.why: The middle size matches control.icon-md, the glyph on a key, with dots at two thirds of the pitch.

lg.why: The large size adds one module step to control.icon-md so the matrix pitch stays on the grille's ratio.

dot.why: Every hole of the 7 × 7 field is drawn and only the glyph's own holes are lit, the Grille's field at icon scale, so one glyph can turn into another (R-008).

data-on.why: A lit hole is a dot of the current glyph; an unlit one waits sunk in its hole at motion.dot-scale and no opacity.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under Reduce motion the dots keep their size and only fade, on motion.hover.

opacity.why: A new glyph morphs. Dots it shares with the last one stay lit, the others fade out over motion.exit on the accelerating curve and new ones fade in over motion.release on the decelerating one (D-008, R-008).

transform.why: A dot that goes sinks back into its hole to motion.dot-scale, and one that comes rises out of it, so a play key turning to pause reads as the same printed field changing.
